subject: Client adapter crash causing elevated errors and latency
messages:
From: Michael Zhao <michael.zhao@acme-retail.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@peakstream.io
Date: 2026-11-15T08:17:00Z
Subject: High error rate and adapter crash in production (request id 0d9f8a)

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing a spike in 5xxs and latency on our checkout flows around 07:52 UTC. Our monitoring shows the Redwood client adapter process on our side is crashing under heavy concurrency and clients are retrying, which is driving request amplification and higher latency. Attached is a short crash log and a heap snapshot.

Error summary:
- Start time: 2026-11-15T07:52:14Z
- Impact: ~18% error rate for requests proxied to /v1/generate, latency P95 jumped from 120ms -> 1.8s
- Request id observed in logs: 0d9f8a
- SDK: redwood-client-java v1.2.3 (we pinned during last deploy)

Sample from crash_log_11-15.txt:
---
Exception in thread "redwood-client-io-7": java.lang.NullPointerException at com.redwood.client.parser.StreamingParser.handleFrame(StreamingParser.java:142)
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: fragment length mismatch
---

Can you triage? This is affecting our checkout conversion and leadership is already flagged. We can provide deeper dumps if needed.

Thanks,
Michael
Michael Zhao
Director of Engineering, Acme Retail
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Zhao <michael.zhao@acme-retail.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T09:04:00Z
Subject: Re: High error rate and adapter crash in production (request id 0d9f8a)

Michael — thanks for the details and the logs, we appreciate the quick heads-up. I'm opening this as a P0 with the infra and client runtime teams.

Immediate next steps:
- Rishi and Karthik are looking at the crash stack and will attempt a quick repro against v1.2.3 to see if we can reproduce under load.
- Stephanie will own coordination with your Ops team for any temporary mitigations (canary toggles, client pin to older adapter).
- If acceptable, we'd like to run a lightweight canary patch on a subset of requests that disables the streaming parser optimizations to see if that removes the crash. This can be toggled without a full deploy.

Can you confirm the safest 15-minute window we could run a canary (low traffic) and whether you can share a pcap or TCP-level fragment from 07:52? That would help confirm if we’re seeing split headers or malformed frames.

Looping in Rishi, Karthik, and Stephanie.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T10:26:00Z
Subject: Re: High error rate and adapter crash in production (internal triage)

Team — quick note from initial investigation. I repro'd a similar NPE locally with our integration test harness when running the Java adapter (v1.2.3) with a synthetic burst (200 concurrent streams) and small MTU / connection churn. The stack matches Michael's crash_log.

Findings so far:
- Root cause appears to be a race in our StreamingParser when handling interleaved chunk headers under backpressure. Under certain timing the parser processes an incomplete header and assumes a non-null header buffer, causing NPE.
- The error is amplified by aggressive connection reuse + HTTP/1.1 keep-alive batching on the client side; partial-fragmented frames arrive across reads and our parser's header-assembly code has a regression introduced in v1.2.0 (optimizations for header coalescing).
- Repro steps: run adapter v1.2.3, simulate 200 concurrent requests with 256B frames and random delays (10–60ms) between packets. Observed parser.throwNPE ~60% of runs.

Temporary mitigations tested (low-effort):
1) Disable header coalescing in adapter config (client-side flag) — stops the NPE but increases CPU by ~7% and increases median latency by ~30ms.
2) Force new connections per request (no pooling) — stops the issue but is not sustainable (increases sockets massively).
3) Roll back to adapter v1.1.8 — no crash observed in repro.

Proposed plan:
- Offer Acme a quick rollback to v1.1.8 or push a config toggle to disable coalescing immediately as a short-term mitigation.
- Patch the parser (add robust header-fragment buffering and checks) and release v1.2.4 within 48 hours with a canary.
- In parallel, add a non-blocking fallback path to avoid NPEs if header state is inconsistent.

I can have a minimal patch in the next 6–8 hours for internal validation.

Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Zhao <michael.zhao@acme-retail.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T14:42:00Z
Subject: Re: High error rate and adapter crash in production (action & mitigation)

Michael — quick update and proposed immediate action.

What we found: Rishi reproduced the crash and traced it to a header-assembly regression in the Java adapter v1.2.x series under high concurrency and small-fragment packets. This causes the streaming parser to dereference a null header buffer in rare timing windows which leads to the adapter process crash you saw.

Short-term options (please pick one so we can act immediately):
A) We push a config toggle to your fleet to disable header coalescing (zero-deploy, server-side toggle). This reduces the crash risk immediately; expected trade-offs: +7% CPU, +30ms median latency.
B) We coordinate you rolling back the adapter to v1.1.8 (we can assist) — low risk but requires a client deploy on your side.
C) We push a hotfix canary that adds safe guards in the parser but keeps coalescing enabled. This will be a controlled canary (5% of traffic) and we expect to promote if green. ETA for patch validation: ~8–12 hours.

Recommendation: start with A while we validate C. If you prefer rollback (B) we’ll support the rollout.

Next steps I need from you: a 15-minute maintenance window this afternoon (US-PST) to toggle A if you approve, and a contact phone number for an on-call engineer.

Apologies for the disruption — we’ll treat this with executive priority until resolved.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference
